CALLCENTER-CTX-I1.title: Support floor office notes Q4
CALLCENTER-CTX-I1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT FLOOR - OFFICE NOTES, FOURTH QUARTER

Holiday party: Saturday 12 December at Marlow Hall, doors at 6:30 pm. Sign up for a potluck dish on the sheet by the kitchen. Vegetarian and nut-free dishes are especially needed.

Parking: Level B garage permits renew by 30 October. Bring your badge to the facilities desk. The bike racks near the east entrance are being repainted, so use the north racks until 8 October.

Cafeteria: Tuesday is chili and cornbread, Thursday is baked pasta. The coffee machine on floor 3 is out of order until the replacement arrives next week.

Fire drill: Wednesday 14 October at 10:30 am. Meet at the assembly point by the loading dock and check in with your floor warden.

Laptop refresh: new laptops go to Team Cedar first, then Team Birch. IT will email your pickup slot.

Head office closure: the head office administration wing is closed on 26 and 27 November and from 25 December to 1 January. The support floor rota is posted separately by team leads.

Lost and found: a blue umbrella, two water bottles, and a single green glove are waiting at reception.

Friday jeans day continues for anyone who drops a dollar in the food bank jar.

CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.title: Halden Home support knowledge base excerpt
CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT KNOWLEDGE BASE - AGENT REFERENCE
Revision 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Halden Home sells fiber internet, mobile plans, and the Halden Box subscription.

1. VERIFICATION
Standard verification is required before discussing any account detail. Collect all of the following: the full name on the account, the 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code. If the customer cannot recall the PIN, the agent may send a one-time code, valid for 10 minutes, to the mobile number or email registered on the account. Agents must never read out, hint at, or confirm a PIN. Agents must never ask a customer to read out a password and must never ask for a full card number.
Changes to email, phone number, password, or shipping address need enhanced verification: the customer must read back the one-time code sent to the contact on file. If the customer has lost access to the registered email, the code goes to the registered mobile number. If neither is available, the customer submits the Identity Review form (photo ID plus a bill from the last 60 days), which is reviewed within 3 business days.
Agents never disclose details of any account other than the verified one, even to a spouse or relative, unless that person is a listed Authorized User.

2. REFUNDS AND RETURNS
Halden Box charges: refundable within 14 days of the charge date if the box has not shipped. Once shipped, the refund is issued after the items are returned.
Devices: 30-day return window from the delivery date. Opened devices carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Defective devices carry no fee.
Duplicate charges: refunded in full with no fee when reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund posts to the original payment method within 5 business days; the customer's bank may take 2 to 3 further business days.
Any refund over $75 needs Tier 2 approval before it is submitted.

3. CANCELLATION
Month-to-month plans can be cancelled at any time. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period with no fee. There are no partial-month refunds except for duplicate charges.
Retention: one offer per customer every 12 months, 2 months at 30 percent off. Offer it once, and only after the customer says they want to cancel.

4. SHIPPING
Standard delivery is 3 to 5 business days after dispatch. If an order has not arrived 7 business days after dispatch, offer a free reship or a refund.
Package marked delivered but missing: ask the customer to check with neighbors and the building office for 24 hours, then open a carrier trace, which takes 3 business days. After the trace, reship or refund.
Wrong item: send a prepaid return label and ship the replacement within 2 business days. Items valued under $20 do not need to be returned.

5. CONNECTIVITY TROUBLESHOOTING
Router light: solid white means online, blinking amber means no line detected, solid red means a hardware fault.
Steps: (1) power cycle for 30 seconds and wait 2 minutes; (2) check cables and test with a wired connection; (3) run the remote line test, about 90 seconds. If the line test fails, book a technician visit within 3 to 5 days. The visit is free when the fault is on the Halden side and $49 when the fault is in the customer's own wiring or equipment.
Configuration of third-party routers, VLANs, and port forwarding is not supported. Agents may share the public setup guide only.

6. OUTAGE STATUS (as of 09:15 today)
Incident INC-4471: fiber outage in the Ridgemont zone, ZIP codes 30411 and 30412. Started 08:40. Estimated restoration 15:30. Estimates are not guarantees and agents must never promise a time. The automatic outage credit of $1.50 per day applies only when an outage lasts longer than 24 hours.

7. ESCALATION LADDER AND CREDIT AUTHORITY
Tier 1 agent: goodwill credit up to $25.
Tier 2 specialist: credits up to $75, billing exceptions, and any customer contacting for the third time about the same issue.
Team lead: credits up to $250. Handles customers who ask for a manager, after the agent has attempted resolution. Callback within 4 business hours.
Duty manager: legal threats, regulatory complaints, suspected account takeover, and credits above $250.
For suspected account takeover, lock the account first, then notify the duty manager.

8. PRIVACY REQUESTS
Data export and deletion requests are handled only through the Privacy Portal. Agents cannot perform them by phone and cannot confirm what data is held. Response takes up to 30 days.

9. CLOSING A CALL
Recap the resolution and next steps, give the reference number, and note that a follow-up email arrives within 1 hour.

CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.title: Refunds and escalations (migrated wiki page)
CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.text:
HALDEN HOME KNOWLEDGE BASE - REFUNDS AND ESCALATIONS
Page status: migrated from the old wiki. Sections marked (v2) were written in 2025 and sections marked (v3) in 2026. Both versions are currently visible to agents.

A. Halden Box refund window (v2)
A subscription box charge can be refunded within 14 days of the charge date. After 14 days no refund is available, only a goodwill credit.

B. Duplicate charges (v2)
If a customer is billed twice for the same box, the second charge is refunded in full within 3 business days of the report. Business days are Monday to Friday.

C. Manager requests (v2)
When a customer asks for a manager, transfer to a team lead immediately. Do not try to resolve the issue first.

D. Halden Box refund window, customer FAQ (v3)
Customers may request a refund on a subscription box within 30 days of the charge date. Agents should follow the FAQ when a customer quotes it.

E. Duplicate charges (v3)
Duplicate charges are refunded in full within 7 business days. For this purpose business days include Saturday. Refunds over $75 need Tier 2 approval before they are submitted.

F. Manager requests (v3)
Before a team lead is contacted, the agent must make at least two documented attempts to resolve the issue. Requests made in anger are handled the same way. The team lead calls the customer back within one business day.

G. Goodwill credits
Tier 1 agents can issue goodwill credits up to $25. Customers with more than 24 months of tenure may receive up to $40 when the floor supervisor on shift approves it.

H. Opened devices
Opened devices returned within 30 days carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Loyalty members may have the fee waived, as applicable. The fee is 15 percent for devices returned after day 30 where an exception has been granted.

I. Cancellations
A cancellation takes effect immediately and the customer loses access at once (v2). A cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period (v3). Check which one applies before confirming with the customer.

J. Duty manager
Legal threats go to the duty manager. Regulatory complaints go to the duty manager at the agent's discretion.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Random question, is it true you guys are moving offices?
items.answer: I don't have anything on an office move, so I can't confirm that. What I can tell you is the head office admin wing is closed on 26 and 27 November and again from 25 December to 1 January, but that's a closure, not a move. If you need the definitive answer, I'd check with facilities or your team lead.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I opened it but it's not what I expected. Can I still send it back?
items.answer: I can help with that. First I need to verify the account, so could you give me the full name on the account, your 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code? Once I've got that, tell me whether it's a device or the Halden Box, and whether it's opened, and I'll confirm the return window and any fee that applies.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Should I be worried about my other accounts too?
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): Someone logged into my account from another country.

NATIVELY: I'm sorry, that's alarming, and we'll treat it as a possible compromise. First, let's secure the account: change your password now from a device you trust, and turn on two-factor authentication if it isn't already on. Then check your recent activity and sign out of all other sessions. Can you tell me whether you still have access to the account right now?
CUSTOMER (heard): Did they see my card details?

NATIVELY: I can't tell you for certain whether they saw your card details, so let's check. Open your payment methods and recent orders, and tell me if there's any charge or saved card you don't recognize.
items.answer: Yes, it's worth checking. If you reused that same password anywhere else, change it on those accounts too, and turn on two-factor authentication wherever it's offered. Start with your email, since that's usually the key to resetting everything else.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: How long will this take?
items.answer: It depends on the issue, so let me not guess. Give me a quick sense of what you're seeing and when it started, and I'll tell you right away whether we can fix it on this call or whether it needs to go to the next tier.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Is there anything else I should know?
items.answer: Nothing else I need to flag right now. If anything changes on my end, I'll let you know. Otherwise, I think we're set.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: The status page says three thirty. Do I get any credit for being down all day?
items.answer: I can see the Ridgemont fiber outage on the status page, and I'm sorry you've been down all day. The automatic outage credit is $1.50 per day, but it only applies once an outage runs longer than 24 hours, so it wouldn't kick in for today. What I can do is apply a goodwill credit to your account for the trouble. Can you confirm the full name on the account and your 6-digit PIN so I can pull it up?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I cancelled my box two weeks ago and I just got charged again. I also see last month's charge was higher than usual, and I want to know if I can get all of it back or if I'm stuck.
items.answer: I'm sorry about that, and I want to get this sorted. Before I can look at the account, I need to verify you: the full name on the account, your 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the card on file or your billing ZIP code. Once that's done I can pull up both charges and tell you exactly what's refundable.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: So it's not just my house?
conversation: CUSTOMER: Hi, my internet is completely down.
USER (spoken): I'm sorry about that. Can I get your full name and ZIP code to verify the account?
CUSTOMER: Sam Okafor, three zero four one one.
USER (spoken): Thanks Sam, you're verified. I can see a known fiber outage in your area, and the status board lists an estimated restoration of three thirty this afternoon.
items.answer: It's not just your house, Sam. This is a known fiber outage affecting your area, so other customers are down too. The status board shows an estimated restoration of three thirty this afternoon. I'll stay on the line with you until it's back up.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: What do you think?
items.answer: I think the direction is right, but I'd want to see the details before I commit to it. What matters most to me is whether it actually solves the problem we're trying to solve, and whether it holds up once we're using it day to day. So my honest answer is that I like where it's heading, and I'd want to walk through the specifics together before we lock anything in.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I don't care that he's busy.
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): Get me your manager.

NATIVELY: I can get a manager on the line for you. Before I do, can you tell me what's happened so far and what outcome you're looking for? That way I can either fix it right now or bring in the right person with the full picture.
items.answer: I hear you, and I'm not going to stall you on that. I just need two things before I hand this off so the manager can actually act: what happened, and what you want done. Give me that and I'll get them on the line now.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: caller wants help setting up a third party VPN on his router, do we support that
items.answer: Whether we support a third party VPN on your router depends on the router model and the firmware it's running, so let me check that first. Can you tell me the make and model of your router, and whether you're on our standard firmware or a custom build?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Who should own this?
items.answer: That depends on what we're talking about, so let me make sure I've got the right thing. If you mean who should take the lead on this issue, I'd say the person closest to it who can actually make the change, with me coordinating so nothing falls through.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: What are you going to do so it doesn't happen a third time?
conversation: CUSTOMER: I ordered the black doorbell camera two-pack, order ending 5512.
USER (spoken): Thanks, I can see that order. What showed up?
CUSTOMER: A white single one. Same mix-up as the replacement last month.
USER (spoken): I'm sorry about that, let me look at what was shipped.
CUSTOMER (heard): That's twice you've got it wrong.

NATIVELY: I hear you, and twice is twice, so let's get this fixed properly rather than just sending another replacement. I'm pulling up what was actually shipped on order 5512 and the last replacement, and I'll confirm what I find before we decide the next step.
items.answer: I'm going to check what was actually picked and packed on both shipments, because two wrong items in a row usually means the same thing went wrong twice. Once I see that, I'll fix the root cause on the order itself, not just ship another replacement, and confirm with you before anything goes out.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: You charged me twice for the same box. I want the extra one back today, not next week, I want confirmation by email before I hang up, and I want to know why it happened.
items.answer: I'm sorry about the double charge, and I understand you want this fixed today. Let me pull up your account and look at the two charges right now. Can you give me the order number or the email on the account so I can find them?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: How long until I actually see it back?
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): I got charged twice for the same box this month.

NATIVELY: I'm sorry about that, let's get it sorted. First I need to verify the account: can you give me the full name on the account, your 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code?
items.answer: It posts to your original payment method within 5 business days, and your bank can take another 2 to 3 business days after that. I'll confirm the exact date once I've verified the account.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Hello? Are you there?
items.answer: Yes, I'm here, sorry about that. Thanks for your patience. Can you hear me clearly now?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: What would you recommend?
items.answer: I'd start with the option that's simplest to run day to day, then check it against what you actually need before committing. If you tell me the one outcome that matters most here, I can point you to a specific recommendation rather than a general one.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: That's twice you've got it wrong.
conversation: CUSTOMER: I ordered the black doorbell camera two-pack, order ending 5512.
USER (spoken): Thanks, I can see that order. What showed up?
CUSTOMER: A white single one. Same mix-up as the replacement last month.
USER (spoken): I'm sorry about that, let me look at what was shipped.
items.answer: I hear you, and twice is twice, so let's get this fixed properly rather than just sending another replacement. I'm pulling up what was actually shipped on order 5512 and the last replacement, and I'll confirm what I find before we decide the next step.

items.question: Can you guarantee it?
items.answer: I can't guarantee it, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I can commit to is the specific outcome we've agreed on, and I'll flag anything that puts it at risk as soon as I see it.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: That doesn't sound right to me.
items.answer: That's fair, let me make sure I've got it right. Can you tell me which part doesn't line up for you, the number itself or how I got to it? Once I know that, I can walk back through what I'm seeing and we'll sort out where we're reading it differently.
